Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that a woman once said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "My husband stands in salaah all night and fasts all day." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to her, "Are you instructing me to stop him from performing salaah at night and from fasting during the day?" She then went away, but returned some time later with the same complaint. Hadhrat Umar (RA) again repeated what he had said the first time. However, Hadhrat Ka'b bin Soor pointed out, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! She has a right." "What is her right?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. Hadhrat Ka'b replied, "Allaah has permitted four wives for him, so count her as one of four. She is therefore entitled to one night in every four nights and one day in every four days." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then summoned the husband and instructed him to spend one of every four nights with her and to skip a fast in every four fasts. [^2]
The Incident of Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) once led Hadhrat Ibn Arqam by the hand to his wife and asked her, "Do you hate me." "Yes I do," she replied. "What made you do this?" Hadhrat Ibn Arqam (RA) asked. Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) explained, "People have been saying too many things about me." When Hadhrat Ibn Arqam (RA) reported the matter to Hadhrat Umar (RA), the Ameerul Mu'mineen called for Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) and asked, "What made you do that?" Again Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) replied, "People have been saying too many things about me." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sent for the wife. She arrived with the shrewd aunt of hers who told her, "When he questions you (about your curt statement), say, 'Because he made me say it on oath, I did not like to tell a lie.'" (When she came before him) Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "What made you say what you did?" She replied, "Because he made me say it on oath, I did not like to tell a lie." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Why not? One of you ought to lie and say something nice because every home is not built on love. Many homes are built on polite interaction stemming from social status and Islaam." [^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Aatika (RA) the Daughter of Hadhrat Zaid bin Amr (RA)

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Aatika (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl (RA) was married to Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). He loved her very much and even gave her an orchard on condition that she does not remarry after his death. He was struck by an arrow during the battle at Taa'if
